sources.source: Crime outcomes in England and Wales 2025 to 2026
sources.verified_fact: The official 23 July 2026 release reports that 26.3% of sexual offences recorded in the year ending March 2026 had no assigned outcome at year end. It also reports that 41.4% of violence against the person offences were closed because victims did not support police action.
sources.quality_effect: Adds investigation-outcome context with open-case, victim-support, offence-mix and later-revision guards; year-end outcomes and charge rates are not offence prevalence or parcel-level safety measurements.

sources.source: Police use of force statistics, England and Wales: April 2024 to March 2025 (second edition)
sources.verified_fact: The second edition records 812,447 use-of-force reports, 9% more than the previous year. One report represents one officer's use of force on one person and may include multiple tactics; the release was revised on 4 June 2026 after revised Derbyshire Police data.
sources.quality_effect: Adds police-force activity context with report-versus-person, multiple-tactic, recording-improvement, BTP-coverage and revision guards; report totals are not unique incidents or neighbourhood risk.

sources.source: Deaths during or following police contact report, 2024/25
sources.verified_fact: The official report records 26 road-traffic fatalities, 2 fatal police shootings, 17 deaths in or following police custody, 60 apparent suicides following custody and 50 other deaths following police contact that were independently investigated.
sources.quality_effect: Adds police-contact safeguarding context while preserving category definitions, referral completeness, independent-investigation selection and annual volatility; categories cannot be summed into a comparable local risk rate.

sources.source: Crime Severity Score: Year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The 9 December 2025 dataset provides Crime Severity Score data for police force areas and Community Safety Partnerships. The method weights police-recorded offences using sentencing information and divides weighted totals by resident population.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a severity-weighted area comparison while retaining police-recording, sentencing-weight, resident-population, transient-population and geography guards; CSS is not an observed parcel-level harm score.

sources.source: Drug misuse in England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited Crime Survey for England and Wales release estimates that 8.7% of people aged 16 to 59, around 2.9 million people, used any drug in the previous 12 months; the change from the previous year was not statistically significant.
sources.quality_effect: Adds survey-prevalence context with age-band, self-report, sampling, statistical-significance and frequency-versus-dependence guards; it is distinct from seizures, arrests and parcel-level drug-market exposure.

sources.source: Homicide in England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited Homicide Index release records 522 homicide victims and a rate of 8.6 per million population in the year ending March 2025. It separately records 508 homicide incidents and warns that low volumes and regional subgroup counts fluctuate.
sources.quality_effect: Adds serious-violence context with victim-versus-incident, recording-year, low-volume, multiple-victim-event, investigation and court-revision guards; national or regional homicide rates are not parcel measurements.

sources.source: Fraud and computer misuse in England and Wales: year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The corrected 26 March 2026 release estimates 4.2 million fraud incidents, 31% more than the previous survey year, and about 692,000 computer-misuse incidents, 32% fewer. ONS corrected commentary on 10 April 2026 and warns that recorded-fraud trends are affected by under-reporting and reporting-body membership.
sources.quality_effect: Adds cyber and fraud context with survey-versus-recorded, reporting-system, correction, reimbursement and category guards; national incident estimates are not local exposure or parcel-level connectivity risk.
